securitysettingssection.these_controls_define_what_risky: These controls define what risky capabilities PinchTab exposes.
securitysettingssection.one_or_more_sensitive_endpoint_families: One or more sensitive endpoint families are enabled. Features like script execution, downloads, uploads, and live capture can expose high-risk capabilities. Only enable them in trusted environments. You are responsible for securing network access, authentication, and downstream use.
securitysettingssection.these_endpoint_families_can_expose_high: These endpoint families can expose high-risk capabilities when enabled. Only turn them on in trusted environments, and only when you accept responsibility for network access, authentication, and downstream use.
securitysettingssection.controls_whether_the_corresponding: Controls whether the corresponding endpoint family is enabled.
securitysettingssection.comma_separated_domain_allowlist_for: Comma-separated domain allowlist for web content. Use exact hosts or patterns like *.example.com.
securitysettingssection.keep_this_list_narrow_empty_or_wildcard: Keep this list narrow. Empty or wildcard entries weaken the main IDPI boundary. Allowing non-local or non-trusted sites increases browser attack surface even when IDPI is enabled.
securitysettingssection.comma_separated_cidrs_or_ips_whose: Comma-separated CIDRs or IPs whose browser-reported remote IP should be trusted during navigation. Use this only for known internal proxies.
securitysettingssection.this_weakens_navigation_ip_checks_for: This weakens navigation IP checks for matching remote IPs. Prefer specific proxy addresses over broad private ranges. Bare IP entries are treated as single hosts.
securitysettingssection.comma_separated_cidrs_or_ips_that_a: Comma-separated CIDRs or IPs that a hostname may resolve to during navigation preflight. This is intended for internal DNS or proxy setups.
securitysettingssection.this_allows_hostnames_to_resolve_to_non: This allows hostnames to resolve to non-public IPs. Keep the list narrow and only include infrastructure you control. Bare IP entries are treated as single hosts.

networksettingssection.http_port_for_the_dashboard_process: HTTP port for the dashboard process.
networksettingssection.network_interface_the_dashboard_process: Network interface the dashboard process binds to. Keeping 127.0.0.1 or localhost limits direct reachability to the local machine.
networksettingssection.a_non_loopback_bind_is_a_documented_non: A non-loopback bind is a documented, non-default, security-reducing configuration change. It may expose the server beyond the local machine unless another network boundary still restricts access. Keep a token set and review proxy or port-publishing behavior explicitly.

networksettingssection.no_token_configured_set_one_through_the: No token configured. Set one through the CLI or config file.
networksettingssection.token_configured_manage_rotation: Token configured. Manage rotation through the CLI or config file; the current value is never returned by the server. Run

networksettingssection.no_api_token_is_set_anyone_who_can: No API token is set. Anyone who can reach this server can access exposed endpoints. Keep it on trusted local networks only, or configure a strong token through the CLI or config file. You are responsible for protecting access.
networksettingssection.base_state_path_used_by_managed_child: Base state path used by managed child instances.
networksettingssection.trust_x_forwarded_proto_x_forwarded: Trust X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Host, and Forwarded headers for origin checks. Enable only when PinchTab runs behind a trusted reverse proxy (e.g. Caddy, nginx).
networksettingssection.controls_whether_dashboard_session: Controls whether dashboard session cookies require HTTPS. Auto enables Secure only on HTTPS. Force Secure is appropriate when TLS is in front of PinchTab.

networksettingssection.keep_dashboard_login_sessions_across: Keep dashboard login sessions across server restarts. Disable this if you want every restart to force a fresh login.
networksettingssection.how_long_an_unused_dashboard_session: How long an unused dashboard session stays valid. This is stored in seconds in config.
networksettingssection.absolute_lifetime_for_a_dashboard: Absolute lifetime for a dashboard session before it must be re-created, even if active.
networksettingssection.ask_for_api_token_re_entry_before: Ask for API token re-entry before saving backend config changes. Disabled by default.
networksettingssection.permit_attaching_pinchtab_to_externally: Permit attaching PinchTab to externally managed Chrome sessions.
networksettingssection.comma_separated_host_allowlist_for: Comma-separated host allowlist for attach requests. Only include hosts you control and trust. Using "*" disables host allowlisting.
networksettingssection.is_a_documented_non_default_security: is a documented, non-default, security-reducing override. It disables host allowlisting entirely and allows remote attach requests to any reachable host with an allowed scheme. Use it only on isolated, operator-controlled networks.
networksettingssection.hosts_in_this_allowlist_may_be_used_for: Hosts in this allowlist may be used for remote attach requests. Broad or untrusted entries expand the trust boundary and can expose external Chrome sessions and browser contents.

allowNetworkIntercept.lets_agents_install_rules_to_abort_or: Lets agents install rules to abort or fulfill (mock) HTTP requests on a tab. When on, response forgery is FORBIDDEN on hosts in 'Allowed websites' below and PERMITTED elsewhere. Forging responses on hosts you've authorized the agent to use (e.g. your bank) is the highest-risk outcome — that's why allowlisted hosts are protected, not the reverse. OPTIONS preflights are skipped by default to avoid breaking CORS.

allowFileScheme.lets_agents_open_local_file_urls_a_file: Lets agents open local file:// URLs. A file:// URL has no host, so it is NOT limited by 'Allowed websites' below and bypasses SSRF/private-IP protection — enabling it grants read access (via snapshot/screenshot/scrape) to any local file the server process can read. It stays blocked while a strict-mode allowlist is active. Enable only on trusted, single-tenant machines.
